title: Half a terabyte, or one line
predict: Both lookups find ball, a word halfway down the file. How much does each one read?
caption: The scan reads about 500 GB to reach a word halfway down the file, and every request pays it again. The index is a short scan of words and offsets, then one pointed read of one line.

title: Two pointers, one pass
predict: The dictionary has seven words and the changelog three. How many times does each pointer move, and does either ever go back?
caption: The smaller word is written and its pointer moves; on a match the changelog's meaning wins and both move. Each pointer moves once per entry, so one pass builds a sorted new file.

title: Same path vs a rolling deployment
predict: Same new file, two ways to switch. In which one does a user ever get bytes from the middle of another word?
caption: At the same path, servers read the new file with last week's offsets and serve garbage until each reloads. With a new path, meta.json and a rolling deployment, answers are briefly mixed but never garbage.

title: One file, one map
predict: Four puts and a delete. Which offset does K1 point to at the end, and where is K2?
caption: Every put, update and delete is appended at the end, then the map points the key at its latest entry: K1 moves to O4 and K2 leaves the map. A get is one lookup and one read.

title: Keep it under the cap
predict: Halve the merge frequency. Does the peak go up or down, and what is the line it must never cross?
caption: Disk usage climbs with writes and drops at each merge. Merge too often and the CPU is busy collecting garbage; too rarely and a peak hits the 1 TB cap. Tune merge frequency and file size by watching the sawtooth.
